purpose: Define expiry as an eligibility/lifecycle state and purge as a separate explicitly authorized destructive operation with exact scope, retention checks and audit evidence.

owns: DWH Expiry and Purge Boundary semantics

topics.name: DWH Expiry and Purge Boundary
topics.purpose: Define expiry as an eligibility/lifecycle state and purge as a separate explicitly authorized destructive operation with exact scope, retention checks and audit evidence.

semantics.expiry_rule: Expiry marks data as past an explicit retention/availability threshold; it does not itself mean physical destruction.
semantics.purge_rule: Purge is a distinct destructive operation targeting exact data/revision/artifact identities.
semantics.validation_rule: Purge validates applicable retention, hold, relation, lineage/audit and policy constraints before destruction.
semantics.authorization_rule: Purge requires explicit destructive-operation authorization independent from ordinary update/delete where policy requires.
semantics.tombstone_rule: Tombstone/audit evidence may remain according to retention/audit profile without retaining purged content.
semantics.cascade_rule: Purge of derived/cached/materialized data never silently purges upstream source.
semantics.failure_rule: Partial/failed purge state is explicit and cannot be represented as complete.

invariants.rule: Retention, archival, expiry, purge and hold state are explicit lifecycle semantics over exact data identities; time passage, storage movement or archive location never silently deletes, declassifies, transfers ownership or restores data.

references.purpose: Expiry derives from explicit retention policy.
Purge is stronger than ordinary delete/tombstone semantics.

prose.summary: Define expiry as an eligibility/lifecycle state and purge as a separate explicitly authorized destructive operation with exact scope, retention checks and audit evidence.
